GET /v1/trust-frameworks.description: List governed platform catalog and tenant custom trust frameworks. You use a framework slug when you register a trusted issuer. The response is a bare JSON array of framework objects.

200.description: A bare JSON array of trust framework objects.

id.description: You receive the stable UUID for this trust framework.

slug.description: You use this URL-safe identifier in the `framework` field when you register a trusted issuer.

name.description: You receive the display name for the framework.

region.description: You receive the region or jurisdiction for the framework.

profile.description: You receive the interoperability profile for the framework.

formats.description: You receive credential format identifiers such as `mdoc` or `sd_jwt_vc` for SD-JWT VC (Selective-Disclosure JWT Verifiable Credential).

items.description: You receive one credential format identifier.

description.description: You receive the framework summary shown to API consumers.

custom.description: You receive `true` when the framework is tenant-owned.

editable.description: You receive `true` when you can update or delete the framework.

governed.description: You receive `true` when a governance authority manages the framework.

POST /v1/trust-frameworks.description: Create a custom trust framework for your tenant. You use the returned slug when you register trusted issuers. Governed frameworks are managed by their authority.

name.description: You set the display name for the custom framework.

region.description: You set the region or jurisdiction for the custom framework.

profile.description: You set the interoperability profile for the custom framework.

formats.description: You set the credential formats this framework accepts, such as `sd_jwt_vc` for SD-JWT VC (Selective-Disclosure JWT Verifiable Credential).

items.description: You set one credential format identifier.

description.description: You set the framework summary shown to API consumers.

201.description: The custom trust framework was created.

id.description: You receive the stable UUID for this trust framework.

slug.description: You receive the generated slug for the custom framework.

name.description: You receive the display name for the framework.

region.description: You receive the region or jurisdiction for the framework.

profile.description: You receive the interoperability profile for the framework.

formats.description: You receive credential format identifiers such as `sd_jwt_vc` for SD-JWT VC (Selective-Disclosure JWT Verifiable Credential).

items.description: You receive one credential format identifier.

description.description: You receive the framework summary shown to API consumers.

custom.description: You receive `true` when the framework is tenant-owned.

editable.description: You receive `true` when you can update or delete the framework.

governed.description: You receive `true` when a governance authority manages the framework.

GET /v1/trust-frameworks/{slug}.description: Fetch one trust framework by slug. You use this endpoint to inspect a custom or governed framework before linking it to a trusted issuer.

params.name: slug
params.description: Slug of the trust framework to fetch.

200.description: The trust framework matching the requested slug.

id.description: You receive the stable UUID for this trust framework.

slug.description: You receive the URL-safe identifier for this framework.

name.description: You receive the display name for the framework.

region.description: You receive the region or jurisdiction for the framework.

profile.description: You receive the interoperability profile for the framework.

formats.description: You receive credential format identifiers such as `sd_jwt_vc` for SD-JWT VC (Selective-Disclosure JWT Verifiable Credential).

items.description: You receive one credential format identifier.

description.description: You receive the framework summary shown to API consumers.

custom.description: You receive `true` when the framework is tenant-owned.

editable.description: You receive `true` when you can update or delete the framework.

governed.description: You receive `true` when a governance authority manages the framework.

PATCH /v1/trust-frameworks/{slug}.description: Edit a custom trust framework. You cannot edit governed frameworks because their governance authority manages them.

params.name: slug
params.description: Slug of the custom trust framework to update.

description.description: You set the updated framework summary.

200.description: The custom trust framework was updated.

id.description: You receive the stable UUID for this trust framework.

slug.description: You receive the URL-safe identifier for this framework.

name.description: You receive the display name for the framework.

region.description: You receive the region or jurisdiction for the framework.

profile.description: You receive the interoperability profile for the framework.

formats.description: You receive credential format identifiers such as `sd_jwt_vc` for SD-JWT VC (Selective-Disclosure JWT Verifiable Credential).

items.description: You receive one credential format identifier.

description.description: You receive the framework summary shown to API consumers.

custom.description: You receive `true` when the framework is tenant-owned.

editable.description: You receive `true` when you can update or delete the framework.

governed.description: You receive `true` when a governance authority manages the framework.

403.description: A governed framework cannot be edited.

detail.description: You receive the reason the governed framework cannot be changed.
detail.example: 'eIDAS 2.0 (EUDI)' is a governed framework managed by its governance authority — it cannot be edited or deleted. Create a custom framework instead.

DELETE /v1/trust-frameworks/{slug}.description: Delete a custom trust framework. You cannot delete governed frameworks because their governance authority manages them. A successful deletion returns no response body.

params.name: slug
params.description: Slug of the custom trust framework to delete.

204.description: The custom trust framework was deleted. No response body is returned.

403.description: A governed framework cannot be deleted.

detail.description: You receive the reason the governed framework cannot be deleted.
detail.example: 'ISO/IEC 18013-5 mDL' is a governed framework managed by its governance authority — it cannot be edited or deleted. Create a custom framework instead.

GET /v1/trusted-issuers.description: List the issuers this tenant trusts when verifying presented credentials. Didit ID rejects credentials whose `iss` value does not match an active trusted issuer. The response is a bare JSON array ordered by most recent creation time.

200.description: A bare JSON array of trusted issuer objects for the caller's tenant.

id.description: You receive the UUID for this trusted issuer registry entry.

name.description: You receive the trusted issuer display name.

iss.description: You receive the issuer identifier that credentials must match.

trust_anchor.description: You receive the signing-key anchor type. `https-jwks` resolves through a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint when one is configured.

jwks_uri.description: You receive the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint. The captured value is an empty string when the registry entry does not store one.

did.description: You receive the decentralized identifier for the issuer. The captured value is an empty string when the registry entry does not store one.

status.description: You receive the trust-gate status for this issuer.

added_by.description: You receive the principal that registered this trusted issuer.

framework.description: You receive the associated framework slug, or null when the issuer is not tied to one.

created_at.description: You receive the timestamp when this trusted issuer was registered.

POST /v1/trusted-issuers.description: Register an issuer whose credentials this tenant accepts. Didit ID uses the issuer identifier and trust anchor when it verifies presented credentials. The new entry starts as active.

name.description: You set the trusted issuer display name.

iss.description: You set the issuer identifier that credentials must match.

trust_anchor.description: You set the signing-key anchor type. Use `https-jwks` for a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) based issuer.

framework.description: You set the trust framework slug to associate with this issuer.

id.description: You receive the UUID for the trusted issuer registry entry.

name.description: You receive the trusted issuer display name.

iss.description: You receive the issuer identifier that credentials must match.

trust_anchor.description: You receive the signing-key anchor type. `https-jwks` resolves through a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint when one is configured.

jwks_uri.description: You receive the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint. The captured value is an empty string when the registry entry does not store one.

did.description: You receive the decentralized identifier for the issuer. The captured value is an empty string when the registry entry does not store one.

status.description: You receive the trust-gate status for this issuer.

added_by.description: You receive the principal that registered this trusted issuer.

framework.description: You receive the associated framework slug, or null when the issuer is not tied to one.

created_at.description: You receive the timestamp when this trusted issuer was registered.

PATCH /v1/trusted-issuers/{uuid}.description: Enable or disable a trusted issuer. A disabled issuer stays in the registry but fails the trust gate during credential verification.

params.name: uuid
params.description: UUID of the trusted issuer registry entry to update.

status.description: You set the updated trust-gate status for this issuer.

200.description: The trusted issuer status was updated.

id.description: You receive the UUID for the trusted issuer registry entry.

name.description: You receive the trusted issuer display name.

iss.description: You receive the issuer identifier that credentials must match.

trust_anchor.description: You receive the signing-key anchor type. `https-jwks` resolves through a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint when one is configured.

jwks_uri.description: You receive the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint. The captured value is an empty string when the registry entry does not store one.

did.description: You receive the decentralized identifier for the issuer. The captured value is an empty string when the registry entry does not store one.

status.description: You receive the updated trust-gate status for this issuer.

added_by.description: You receive the principal that registered this trusted issuer.

framework.description: You receive the associated framework slug, or null when the issuer is not tied to one.

created_at.description: You receive the timestamp when this trusted issuer was registered.

DELETE /v1/trusted-issuers/{uuid}.description: Remove an issuer from this tenant's trusted issuer registry. After removal, credentials from this issuer no longer pass the verification trust gate. A successful removal returns no response body.

params.name: uuid
params.description: UUID of the trusted issuer registry entry to remove.

204.description: The trusted issuer was removed. No response body is returned.

POST /v1/trusted-issuers/{uuid}/validate.description: Validate a trusted issuer's trust anchor. Didit ID checks reachability and key resolution. You can use the result before relying on a new or changed issuer.

params.name: uuid
params.description: UUID of the trusted issuer registry entry to validate.

200.description: The trusted issuer object with a validation result.

id.description: You receive the UUID for the trusted issuer registry entry.

name.description: You receive the trusted issuer display name.

iss.description: You receive the issuer identifier that credentials must match.

trust_anchor.description: You receive the signing-key anchor type. `https-jwks` resolves through a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint when one is configured.

jwks_uri.description: You receive the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint. The captured value is an empty string when the registry entry does not store one.

did.description: You receive the decentralized identifier for the issuer. The captured value is an empty string when the registry entry does not store one.

status.description: You receive the trust-gate status for this issuer.

added_by.description: You receive the principal that registered this trusted issuer.

framework.description: You receive the associated framework slug, or null when the issuer is not tied to one.

created_at.description: You receive the timestamp when this trusted issuer was registered.

validation.description: You receive the result of the trust-anchor check.

anchor_ok.description: You receive `true` when key resolution succeeds.

reachable.description: You receive `true` when Didit ID can reach the issuer trust anchor.

status.description: You receive the registry status used during validation.

GET /v1/relying-parties.description: List relying parties registered under this tenant. Didit ID uses each origin when wallet presentation requests flow through the W3C Digital Credentials API. The response is a bare JSON array ordered by most recent creation time.

200.description: A bare JSON array of relying party objects for the caller's tenant.

id.description: You receive the UUID for this relying party registration.

name.description: You receive the relying party display name.

origin.description: You receive the registered web origin for this relying party.

client_id.description: You receive the OpenID4VP (OpenID for Verifiable Presentations) client identifier. The value can be an empty string when you do not set one.

status.description: You receive the registration status for this relying party.

created_at.description: You receive the timestamp when this relying party was registered.

POST /v1/relying-parties.description: Register a relying party verifier origin for wallet presentation requests. Didit ID uses the origin when a request flows through the W3C Digital Credentials API. The new registration starts as active.

name.description: You set the relying party display name.

origin.description: You set the web origin for this relying party.

id.description: You receive the UUID for this relying party registration.

name.description: You receive the relying party display name.

origin.description: You receive the registered web origin for this relying party.

client_id.description: You receive the OpenID4VP (OpenID for Verifiable Presentations) client identifier. The captured value is an empty string when you do not set one.

status.description: You receive the registration status for this relying party.

created_at.description: You receive the timestamp when this relying party was registered.

DELETE /v1/relying-parties/{uuid}.description: Remove a relying party registration from this tenant. After removal, Didit ID no longer recognizes the verifier origin for registered-origin checks. A successful removal returns no response body.

params.name: uuid
params.description: UUID of the relying party registration to remove.

204.description: The relying party registration was removed. No response body is returned.
